overview: Singapore Exchange Limited (SGX Group) operates Singapore's securities exchange, derivatives exchange, and the associated clearing, depository and settlement infrastructure, making it the monopoly regulated market operator and central counterparty for Singapore-listed equities and the regulator (via SGX RegCo) of its own markets. Beyond its home securities market, SGX has built a diversified multi-asset franchise spanning pan-Asian equity derivatives (FTSE China A50, Nikkei 225, GIFT Nifty, FTSE Taiwan), OTC FX, and commodity derivatives (notably the world-leading iron ore derivatives market), supplemented by market data, connectivity/co-location and index (iEdge) revenue. Fiscal year ends June 30; FY2026 (ended 30 June 2026) was a record year with net revenue of S$1,478.3 million and net profit of S$698.4 million.

business_model.summary: SGX earns transaction-based trading and clearing fees across four main segments, supplemented by steadier recurring revenue from market data, connectivity/co-location, listing fees, depository/securities settlement, and treasury income earned on member margin and collateral balances. Trading-linked revenue (cash equities, equity derivatives, FX and commodity derivatives) is inherently cyclical with market volumes and volatility, while market data, connectivity and index licensing provide a more annuity-like revenue base. Treasury income is a smaller but rate-sensitive contributor that has been a headwind as benchmark rates have come down from their 2023-2024 peak.

revenue_streams.name: FICC – Fixed Income, Currencies & Commodities (OTC FX, currency & commodity derivatives, bond listings)
Platform and Others (market data, connectivity/co-location, indices, treasury income)

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional – member firms, global and regional banks, proprietary trading firms, asset managers and institutional investors access SGX markets through trading/clearing members; retail investors participate indirectly through brokers. Issuers (listed companies, bond issuers, ETF/structured product sponsors) are a separate customer base for listing and issuer services.
business_model.geographic_mix: Singapore-domiciled exchange with an internationally oriented client base: SGX describes itself as Asia's most international exchange, with offices across 19 cities (including London, New York, Hong Kong, Mumbai, Shanghai, Tokyo, Dubai) and over 40% of trading members based outside Singapore. Derivatives and FX franchises derive significant volume from China (CNH), India (GIFT Nifty, INR/USD), Japan, Taiwan and broader ASEAN exposure rather than purely domestic Singapore activity.

main_competitors: National/regional exchanges in Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam competing for ASEAN listings and liquidity
competitive_position.market_position: Sole operator of Singapore's cash equities, bonds and depository market, and the leading pan-Asian multi-asset derivatives venue outside of China/Japan/India's domestic exchanges – notably the global leader in iron ore derivatives and a top-3 exchange-backed OTC FX venue by volume. However, in absolute scale SGX is a mid-sized regional exchange: average daily securities turnover of roughly S$1.3-1.8 billion is dwarfed by Hong Kong's HK$20-30 billion+ range, and Singapore's cash equities market has structurally lagged regional peers in new listings.

moat_factors.factor: Regulatory monopoly on SGX-listed securities trading and clearing
moat_factors.description: As the sole licensed securities exchange and central counterparty for Singapore-listed securities and depository (CDP), SGX has no domestic competitor for trading, clearing and settling SGX-listed stocks, bonds, REITs and ETFs – a structural, regulator-granted moat analogous to other national exchange monopolies.

SGX's flagship pan-Asian equity index futures (FTSE China A50, Nikkei 225, GIFT Nifty, FTSE Taiwan) and its iron ore derivatives franchise benefit from classic exchange network effects: liquidity attracts liquidity, and once a benchmark contract becomes the market standard, switching costs for market makers, hedgers and arbitrageurs are very high. Management explicitly frames this as 'first-mover' advantage that is 'hard to shift' once established.

moat_factors.factor: Central counterparty (CCP) clearing infrastructure and capital
moat_factors.description: SGX's clearing houses act as CCP for its derivatives and securities markets, contributing at least 25% of default fund resources from its own capital – among the highest 'skin in the game' of global CCPs. This embeds SGX into the risk infrastructure of every member and creates high switching costs for clearing relationships.

moat_factors.factor: Brand, regulatory standing and Aa2 credit rating
moat_factors.description: SGX's dual role as exchange operator and frontline regulator (SGX RegCo) underpins trust in a jurisdiction with a strong rule-of-law reputation; Moody's reaffirmed an Aa2 rating with stable outlook in November 2024, supporting low funding costs and counterparty confidence.

A decade-long strategy to diversify beyond Singapore cash equities into FX, commodities, fixed income and pan-Asian derivatives reduces reliance on the structurally challenged domestic listings market and lets SGX cross-sell index, data and connectivity products across asset classes.

weaknesses: Heavy reliance on a structurally shrinking domestic listings pipeline: SGX has seen delistings persistently outpace new IPOs in recent years (e.g., roughly 20 delistings versus only a handful of new listings in some years), with about two-thirds of listed companies trading below net tangible asset value, reflecting weak valuations and limited liquidity for small/mid caps

Small absolute scale versus regional and global peers: SGX's average daily securities turnover (~S$1.2-1.8 billion) is a small fraction of Hong Kong's (reported in the tens of billions HKD), limiting its ability to compete head-to-head for large-cap listings and liquidity
Revenue mix still meaningfully linked to trading volumes and volatility, which are cyclical and can reverse sharply in quiet markets, unlike pure subscription/data businesses
Treasury income (earned on member margin/collateral) is a declining, rate-sensitive revenue source as central banks ease policy rates
Execution risk on newer franchises (OTC FX, India/GIFT Nifty, gold and other multi-asset initiatives) that are smaller and less entrenched than the flagship China A50 and iron ore contracts

Dependence on Singapore government/MAS policy support (e.g., Equity Market Development Programme) to revitalise the local listings market, which is a multi-year, uncertain structural fix rather than something SGX fully controls

growth_drivers: SGX FX and OTC FX franchise growth: now among the top three exchange-backed OTC FX venues by volume globally, with headline ADV up ~28-35% in recent periods and expansion to over 200 institutional clients across 12 cities; management is investing in AI/analytics tools and new currency pairs (e.g., Brazilian real via the B3 partnership) to extend reach beyond Asia
Commodities franchise, led by the world-leading iron ore derivatives market, which gained a milestone inclusion in S&P's Dow Jones Commodity Index in 2025, plus growing freight derivatives adoption

Pan-Asian equity derivatives cross-sell: new contract launches (e.g., Micro FTSE Taiwan index futures) and deepening client adoption of GIFT Nifty, India suite and China-themed (CNH, FTSE China A50) products, with total derivatives daily average volume up double digits year-on-year

MAS-led Equities Market Review Group reforms: the S$5-6.5 billion Equity Market Development Programme, a proposed SGX-Nasdaq dual-listing bridge via a new Global Listing Board, shortened IPO approval timelines, and board-lot reductions aimed at reviving Singapore's domestic listings pipeline and IPO funds raised (which rebounded sharply to over S$2 billion in the reform's early stages)
Market data, connectivity and indices (Platform and Others segment) growth via repricing and higher co-location sales, providing a more recurring, less cyclical revenue stream

Bolt-on M&A and strategic partnerships (e.g., Brazil's B3 exchange tie-up for listed FX) to extend SGX's multi-asset, global footprint, balanced against portfolio pruning of non-core assets (SGX sold its Scientific Beta index subsidiary to STOXX/ISS STOXX in 2026 for ~€23 million to sharpen focus on core growth priorities)

Structural dividend growth commitment: management has guided to raising the quarterly dividend by 0.25 cents every quarter through FY2028, alongside medium-term guidance for 6-8% group revenue growth (ex-treasury income)

business.description: Delistings have outpaced new IPOs for multiple consecutive years, with roughly two-thirds of listed companies trading below net tangible asset value; a shrinking, undervalued domestic cash equities market threatens the long-term depth and relevance of SGX's home listings franchise even as derivatives and FICC offset it.

Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing has reasserted IPO leadership (44+ IPOs with over 200 under review in recent periods) and dwarfs SGX's turnover; companies and liquidity can migrate to larger, deeper pools in Hong Kong, mainland China, or elsewhere in ASEAN (Malaysia, Indonesia).

A substantial share of revenue (cash equities and derivatives trading/clearing fees) scales with traded value and contract volumes, which are inherently cyclical and can decline sharply if market volatility and investor engagement normalise after a strong multi-year run.

A meaningful share of equity derivatives revenue depends on a small number of flagship benchmark contracts (FTSE China A50, Nikkei 225, GIFT Nifty, iron ore); any erosion of liquidity leadership in these specific contracts (e.g., to a competing venue or OTC alternative) would disproportionately hurt revenue given the network-effect nature of derivatives liquidity.

financial.description: Treasury income earned on member margin/collateral balances fell as benchmark rates eased; continued global monetary easing would further reduce this revenue stream, a headwind management has explicitly flagged in recent results.

SGX earns revenue across multiple currencies (USD-denominated OTC FX volumes, various Asian currency derivatives) and reports in SGD; currency translation can create modest volatility in reported results.

Sell-side commentary following FY2026 results flagged SGX trading at a significant premium to its historical average P/E (reported around 35-39x FY26 earnings against a ~22-23x five-year average), leaving limited room for multiple expansion and greater sensitivity to any earnings disappointment.

regulatory.risk: Dual role as regulator and commercial operator
regulatory.description: SGX RegCo's frontline regulatory function (listing standards, enforcement, market surveillance) must be seen as credible and independent; any perceived lapse in regulatory standards or a market integrity incident could damage confidence in SGX markets and its competitiveness as a listing venue.

The Equities Market Review Group's reforms (Global Listing Board, SGX-Nasdaq dual-listing bridge, consultation on Securities and Futures Act amendments) are generally supportive for SGX but introduce implementation and timing uncertainty, and could in principle alter competitive dynamics or fee structures as rules are finalised through 2026-2028.
SGX RegCo's new three-year deadline for suspended companies to resolve issues could trigger a wave of further delistings in the near term even as it is intended to improve market quality over time.

macro.risk: Global monetary policy and rate cycle
macro.description: Interest rate levels affect both treasury income (margin/collateral yield) and broader risk appetite driving trading volumes; a global easing cycle is a mixed influence – supportive of trading activity per some management commentary, but a direct drag on treasury income.

Shifting international trade dynamics and geopolitical tension have historically boosted SGX's hedging-related derivatives and FX volumes (a 'volatility is good for exchanges' dynamic), but a sustained, severe macro shock (e.g., a major regional conflict or financial crisis) could instead suppress capital markets activity and listings broadly.

A meaningful share of SGX's derivatives franchise (FTSE China A50, CNH products, India GIFT Nifty) is linked to specific Asian economies; a slowdown or capital control tightening in China or India could reduce demand for these flagship hedging and access products.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global exchange operators are benefiting from a multi-year increase in trading activity amid macro volatility (tariffs/trade policy shifts, divergent central bank policy, geopolitical uncertainty), alongside secular growth in derivatives usage for risk management and continued institutional demand for Asian market access. Singapore specifically is undergoing a government-led push (MAS Equities Market Review Group, Equity Market Development Programme) to revitalise its equities market after years of listings underperformance versus regional peers.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical. Trading and clearing revenue (the majority of group revenue) rises with market volumes and volatility and can soften in calm, low-volume periods; market data, connectivity, listing and depository revenue are comparatively more stable and recurring, providing a partial offset.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate, and double-edged: lower rates reduce treasury income earned on member margin/collateral balances (a direct headwind), but rate-cutting cycles and associated macro uncertainty have historically coincided with higher trading and hedging volumes (an indirect tailwind) per recent management commentary citing the Federal Reserve's easing cycle as supportive of FY2026 volumes.
key_input_costs: Depreciation and amortisation of trading/clearing systems
Data centre and co-location infrastructure costs

recent_developments.event: SGX Group reported record FY2026 (year ended 30 June 2026) results: net revenue of S$1,478.3 million (+13.9% YoY), reported net profit of S$698.4 million (+7.8%), adjusted net profit of S$759.5 million (+24.6%), and adjusted EBITDA of S$980.6 million (+17.9%). Growth was broad-based across all segments: Equities – Cash net revenue +28.1% to S$502.9 million, FICC net revenue +17.0% to S$376.2 million, Equities – Derivatives net revenue roughly flat at S$344.5 million, and Platform and Others net revenue +7.0% to S$254.7 million.

Board proposed a final quarterly dividend of 11.5 cents plus a one-off additional dividend of 12.5 cents (both payable 10 November 2026, subject to AGM approval on 23 October 2026), bringing total FY2026 dividends to 57.0 cents versus 37.5 cents in FY2025 — a large step-up attributed to capital recycling gains and disciplined capital management, on top of the standing policy of raising the quarterly dividend by 0.25 cents each quarter through FY2028.

Management issued medium-term guidance of 6-8% group revenue growth (excluding treasury income) and low-to-mid-single-digit expense growth; for FY2027 specifically, guided expense growth of 6-8% and capital expenditure of approximately S$100 million, with CEO Loh Boon Chye describing SGX as entering FY2027 'from a position of strength' and highlighting strategic index partnerships, new ecosystems (including gold), deeper integration of listed and OTC FX businesses, and data-driven client relationships as priorities.

Phillip Securities downgraded SGX to Neutral despite raising its price target to S$25.00 (from S$18.30), citing a valuation of ~38.6x FY26 earnings versus a ~22x five-year average; the note highlighted FY26 securities daily average value of S$1.8 billion (an 18-year high, +35% YoY) as the key driver of cash equities revenue growth.

Macquarie downgraded SGX to Underperform (from Neutral) and cut its price target to S$20.30, arguing the stock's valuation already reflects a stronger operating base and that the bar for further earnings upside has risen materially after the FY2026 re-rating.

1H FY2026 results (half year ended 31 December 2025) showed net revenue excluding treasury income up 10.1% to S$636.6 million and adjusted net profit up 11.6% to S$357.1 million, with growth led by FICC (+14% revenue) and broad-based volume strength in OTC FX (ADV +32% to US$180 billion) and currency/commodity derivatives, partly offset by a 14% decline in treasury income on lower margin-deposit yields.

SGX Group completed the sale of its Scientific Beta index subsidiary (acquired in 2020 for €186 million) to STOXX (part of ISS STOXX) for approximately €23 million, following a roughly S$15 million net loss (including goodwill impairment) in the unit over 1H FY2026; management framed the divestment as portfolio discipline to sharpen focus on core multi-asset growth priorities while retaining its broader iEdge index platform.

PC Partner Group voluntarily withdrew its Hong Kong Stock Exchange listing while continuing to trade on SGX, cited by local commentators as a rare example of a company consolidating its listing toward Singapore rather than away from it, against the broader backdrop of SGX delistings outpacing IPOs.

The MAS-chaired Equities Market Review Group finalized its reform package, including a proposed SGX-Nasdaq dual-listing bridge via a new SGX Global Listing Board targeting Asian growth companies valued at S$2 billion or more, alongside MAS and SGX RegCo consultation papers on the legislative and listing-rule changes needed to implement it; MAS separately expanded the Equity Market Development Programme from S$5 billion to S$6.5 billion in February 2026.

items.vs_prior: reiterated/formalized as explicit medium-term target alongside FY2026 results
items.notes: Framed as a durable, multi-asset growth target rather than a single-year number; FY2026 actual ex-treasury net revenue growth of 15.0% ran well ahead of this medium-term band.

items.target: 6-8% (low-to-mid-single-digit referenced for medium term; 6-8% specifically guided for FY2027)
items.vs_prior: new guide for FY2027; up from FY2025's commentary of expenses coming in at the lower end of a 2-4% increase guidance range
items.notes: Reflects continued investment in growth initiatives (FX, commodities, technology) even as management emphasises expense discipline.

items.vs_prior: raised from FY2025's guidance of S$70-75 million (which itself came in at the lower end)
items.notes: Step-up in capex supports technology and new product/platform investment across the multi-asset strategy.

items.target: Quarterly dividend increases of 0.25 cents per quarter
items.notes: On top of this baseline growth, FY2026 included a one-off additional 12.5 cents dividend tied to capital recycling gains (e.g., Scientific Beta divestment proceeds), which is not part of the recurring growth policy.
Reflects management's continued framing of SGX FX as a scaling, strategically important but still relatively small contributor within the overall EBITDA base.

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Loh Boon Chye said SGX enters FY2027 'from a position of strength,' with priorities centered on expanding through strategic index partnerships and new ecosystems such as gold, more closely linking the listed and OTC FX businesses, and using data and analytics to deepen client relationships. Management has repeatedly emphasised 'deploying capital with discipline' — balancing continued organic investment and bolt-on M&A (e.g., the B3 exchange partnership) against portfolio pruning of non-core assets (the Scientific Beta divestment) — while reiterating that global capital flows are changing in both direction and structure, which the company believes positions its multi-asset, multi-geography platform favourably.

bull_case: Diversified, multi-asset franchise with genuine moats: a regulatory monopoly on Singapore securities clearing combined with network-effect-driven leadership in specific pan-Asian derivatives (FTSE China A50, iron ore, GIFT Nifty) gives SGX pricing power and resilience that a single-asset exchange would lack

Record FY2026 results demonstrate broad-based momentum across all four segments simultaneously (Equities-Cash +28%, FICC +17%, Platform +7%, Derivatives roughly flat), with SDAV at an 18-year high and OTC FX ADV up 28-35%, suggesting the multi-year multi-asset diversification strategy is compounding rather than simply rotating between segments

Policy tailwind from MAS's Equities Market Review Group reforms (Equity Market Development Programme now S$6.5 billion, SGX-Nasdaq dual-listing bridge, faster IPO approvals) could meaningfully revive the long-moribund Singapore listings pipeline, a call option not fully reflected in a derivatives-and-FX-led bull case

Shareholder-friendly, programmatic capital return: a standing policy of raising the quarterly dividend by 0.25 cents every quarter through FY2028, plus a track record of opportunistic one-off distributions (the FY2026 12.5-cent special dividend) funded by portfolio recycling (Scientific Beta sale)

Low direct cyclicality risk relative to other financials: SGX carries no credit risk on its own balance sheet comparable to a bank, benefits from heightened volatility/hedging demand in uncertain macro environments, and maintains a strong Aa2-rated balance sheet with conservative leverage (~0.9-1.0x) and very high interest coverage (50-110x)
bear_case: Valuation has run well ahead of fundamentals after the FY2026 re-rating: multiple sell-side desks (Phillip Securities, Macquarie, RHB) flagged SGX trading at 35-39x FY26 earnings versus a historical five-year average closer to 22-23x, with Macquarie moving to an explicit Underperform/Sell call on valuation grounds in September 2026

The core domestic listings market remains structurally impaired: delistings have outpaced IPOs for multiple consecutive years, roughly two-thirds of listed companies trade below net tangible asset value, and Singapore's average daily turnover remains a small fraction of Hong Kong's, undermining the long-term depth of SGX's home market even as derivatives and FX carry current growth

Treasury income is a structural headwind in a global easing cycle, and the strong FY2026 volume-driven growth (SDAV, derivatives ADV, OTC FX volumes) may not repeat if market volatility normalises from currently elevated levels, exposing the cyclical nature of the bulk of SGX's revenue base

Execution risk on the MAS-led market reforms: the SGX-Nasdaq dual-listing bridge, Global Listing Board and related legislative changes are still working through consultation and implementation as of late 2026, and a multi-year timeline (12-24 months for the Equity Market Implementation Committee alone) creates risk that the anticipated listings revival disappoints or is delayed

Concentration in a relatively narrow set of flagship derivatives contracts (China A50, iron ore, GIFT Nifty) means that any erosion of liquidity leadership in these specific products, whether from new regional competition or a shift in underlying market structure, would disproportionately impact the derivatives segment given how network-effect-driven exchange liquidity is
